opportunities.description: Yale’s competitive Project Awards provide $50,000 to $500,000 for defined work benefiting New Haven residents. Eligible applicants must be New Haven-based 501(c)(3) nonprofits. Applications are due August 31, 2026 at 5:00 p.m.
opportunities.eligibility: Applicant must be headquartered in New Haven, hold 501(c)(3) status in good standing, serve New Haven residents, manage award funds, provide required records, and submit only one fund application per year.
opportunities.fundingDetails: Project Awards support requests from $50,000 to $500,000. Yale is making $1.5 million available per year for FY2027 through FY2029 across the fund.
opportunities.nextStep: Assess eligibility immediately. If applying, finalize scope, measurable outcomes, budget, sustainability plan, and supporting community evidence before August 31 at 5:00 p.m.
opportunities.notes: High-value local opportunity with an August 31 deadline. AI is not a named category, so it should be presented as a tool supporting community outcomes, not as the project’s sole purpose.

opportunities.description: Yale’s Small Awards provide up to $5,000 for smaller community-centered efforts benefiting New Haven residents. Applications are reviewed monthly while funds remain and must be submitted at least 60 days before the activity. Eligible applicants must be New Haven-based 501(c)(3) nonprofits.
opportunities.eligibility: Applicant must meet the fund’s New Haven headquarters and 501(c)(3) requirements, submit only one fund application per year, and apply at least 60 days before the proposed activity.
opportunities.fundingDetails: Small Awards provide up to $5,000. A separate pool of approximately $100,000 per year is available, subject to remaining funds.
opportunities.nextStep: Develop a small, clearly scoped activity and apply at least 60 days before it begins. Informal leaders should partner with an eligible New Haven nonprofit.
opportunities.notes: Potential fit for community AI workshops, digital-literacy events, materials, short-term hands-on expert help, or participant support when submitted by an eligible nonprofit.
